newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil firms to meet minister over new rules.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil firms to meet minister over new rules.

text.p: Nigeria's foreign joint venture oil production partners are to meet with the petroleum minister on Monday to discuss new rules the companies have warned may increase costs, the majority-state owned Business Times reports.
The newspaper said petroleum minister Dan Etete would give the companies the chance to express their views.

Etete last month publicly accused the joint-venture partners of cheating Nigeria of its fair share of oil wealth and said they would have to set up escrow accounts, which would allow the government to keep a closer eye on where contributions to production and exploration costs were going.
Oil companies officials say if applied the rules could increase production costs, but privately say they think it unlikely Nigeria would strictly enforce rules that could harm it's own industry.
The five major joint ventures are run by subsidiaries of Shell, Mobil, Chevron, Agip and Elf. State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) is the majority partner in all of them.
The OPEC producer pumps around two million barrels of crude per day.
